issues.claim: price_ranges.mid_market: 'About $1.45–$6.00 per door/unit per month for published per-door tools (… Buildium Maintenance Contact Center $0.70–$1.10 per unit)' and one_line: 'published per-door rates run $1.45–$9.99 with $140–$700 monthly minimums'
issues.problem: The range does not follow from the prices listed inside the same sentence: Buildium's Maintenance Contact Center is quoted at $0.70–$1.10 per unit per month (re-confirmed on buildium.com/maintenance-contact-center today), which is below the stated $1.45 floor. The minimum floor is also understated: Latchel's Analytics+ carries a $100/month minimum (third-party, confirmed), below the '$140–$700' band, and Properties Meld's $200 / Vendoroo's $400 / HappiNest's $700 all sit inside it — but $100 does not.
issues.fix: Restate the per-door list-rate range as about $0.70–$6.00 per unit per month (Buildium $0.70–$1.10, HappiNest $1.45–$1.95, Property Meld $2.00 + $1.50 add-on, Vendoroo $3–$6, AppFolio $1.49–$5.00 third-party), or explicitly exclude Buildium's $0.70 'missed maintenance calls' plan as a lower-service human call-center variant and say so. Change the minimum band to $100–$700 and name each floor (Latchel $100, Buildium $140, Property Meld $200, Vendoroo $400, HappiNest $700). Mirror the corrected numbers in one_line.

issues.claim: Property Meld tier 'Core — $1.60 per unit per month (third-party reading; may be dated)'
issues.problem: No source URL is given for the $1.60 figure anywhere in the brief, and the cited source page (propertymeld.com/pricing, re-opened today) shows only Ops at $2.00/unit and MAX On-Call at $1.50/unit. A price with no citation is unsupported even when labelled third-party.
issues.fix: Add the third-party URL that states $1.60/unit with its check date, or delete the Core tier and note that only Ops ($2.00) and MAX On-Call ($1.50) are on the vendor page.

issues.claim: Vendoroo tiers named 'Engage' ($3/door), 'Direct' ($6/door) and 'Command' (custom, '$3 to $8.50 per door')
issues.problem: vendoroo.ai/pricing-vendors, opened today, shows no dollar figures and no Engage/Direct/Command names at all — it currently lists 'Receptionist' and 'Maintenance Coordinator' products plus add-ons. Engage/Direct with the $400 minimum and annual billing is supported only by the third-party rentive.ai guide (checked 30 Sep 2026, which itself cites Vendoroo's pricing page), and no source in the brief mentions a 'Command' tier or 'invoice collection' as an inclusion.
issues.fix: Keep Engage/Direct/$400 minimum/annual billing but label them 'third-party reading, 30 Sep 2026; Vendoroo's live page now shows unnamed Receptionist and Maintenance Coordinator products with no prices'. Drop the 'Command' tier and the 'invoice collection' inclusion, or cite a source that states them; the only confirmed vendor statement is the blog line '$3 to $8.50 per door depending on the package'.

issues.claim: Latchel integrations_included: 'Yardi, Rent Manager, Buildium, Propertyware work-order sync'
issues.problem: The cited page (latchel.com/waitlist/, re-opened today) says only 'Yardi, Rent Manager & other popular integrations'. The third-party directory used for the Analytics+ price lists Yardi and Rent Manager only. Buildium and Propertyware are not stated in either source.
issues.fix: List Yardi and Rent Manager and add 'other integrations not itemised', or cite a Latchel page that names Buildium and Propertyware.

issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy #1: 'At 150 doors a $3/door tool is $450/month …, so a $400–$900/month managed retainer sits inside what buyers already pay for software alone'
issues.problem: Labelled inference, but it contradicts its own arithmetic: at 150 doors the software spend it just computed is $450/month (HappiNest at that size is $700 on its minimum), so only the $400–$700 part of the band sits inside software spend; $900 is roughly double the $450 figure.
issues.fix: Reword to 'a $400–$700/month retainer is in line with, or below, what a 150-door firm already pays for per-door software ($450 at $3/door; $700 on HappiNest's minimum); $900/month needs the human-backup/integration scope to justify it'.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs: 'One commenter recalled EliseAI costing about $50–$60 per property per month with high upfront costs' — year 'undated (older thread)'
issues.problem: The r/CommercialRealEstate thread is blocked to direct fetch (I could not open it), but the search index for that URL dates the comment 24 Oct 2024 and frames it as the commenter's uncertain recollection. 'Undated' misstates the year, and the unit is per property, not per unit, which matters when it is set beside $3–$6/unit figures.
issues.fix: Set year to 2024 (comment date per search index; page itself not retrievable) and state explicitly 'per property per month, commenter unsure'.

issues.claim: what_is_included_vs_extra: 'a per-property AI receptionist can be configured to stay out of lease/legal/rent decisions … the boundary is set during setup, not by the software'
issues.problem: inboundbooking.com/property-management presents this as fixed product behaviour, not configuration: a section headed 'It won't touch the lease' and an FAQ ('It never makes legal, lease, rent or payment decisions') describe a designed exclusion. The 'set during setup, not by the software' framing is the brief's own characterisation and is presented as fact.
issues.fix: Reword to 'this vendor's product excludes legal, lease, rent and payment decisions by design; how far an agent goes in other tools is a setup/configuration decision' or label the generalisation as inference.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs: BiggerPockets 'small operator … found plans starting around $35–$45 per month' — year 'undated forum thread'
issues.problem: The thread (biggerpockets.com/forums/52/topics/756172…) is open and the figure is there ('base plans at $35 to $45 per month', original poster researching services), but the thread is roughly seven years old (posts marked '7y'), not undated. The brief also does not say the $35–$45 is the OP's research rather than an actual bill.
issues.fix: Give the year as c. 2018–2019 (posts show '7y') and note it is a prospective buyer's research, not a paid bill — which weakens its use as a current price datapoint.
